blocks.text: Royal Heights is a small, mostly residential pocket in northwest Surrey, near 96 Avenue and Scott Road, on a hill above the Fraser. People looking at homes for sale in Royal Heights often come for the quiet streets, the views toward New Westminster, the North Shore mountains, and the river, and the short hop to the bridges and major roads.

The City of Surrey says that around Royal Heights Park, most homes were built from the late 1950s to the early 1970s. You will see basement-entry, split-level, and rancher-style houses, with some newer homes and townhouses mixed in. The park was established in the mid-1960s, with a forested side, an open field, and looping trails. A group of lots beside the park was rezoned in 2026 — confirm the current zone with the City.

parts.t: Living in Royal Heights often means a house with a yard. Many homes have a secondary suite, or room for one; always confirm that any suite was built with a permit. Nearby public schools include Royal Heights Elementary and L.A. Matheson Secondary. Check the

blocks.text: Small and self-contained, Royal Heights is an enclave whose story is elevation and views over the lowland. Most of the houses around the park date from the late 1950s to the early 1970s, when the streets were first built.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Royal Heights?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 19 houses listed with 2 sold in the month and 2 condos and townhomes listed with 0 sold in the month in Royal Heights. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Royal Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 11%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
